learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamentals of machine tools, including their economic significance, definition, and classification criteria.
Identify and evaluate the requirements for machine tools.
Apply manual and machine programming of NC-controlled manufacturing facilities in practice.
Design, dimension, and calculate drive systems for machine tools.
Understand measurement systems and working accuracy, and determine positional uncertainty.
Create and apply mathematical models of the dynamic system "machine tool".
Describe and implement the process flow of NC programming.
Identify Teach-in programming, computer-aided workshop programming (WOP), computer-aided AV programming, and CAD programming, and recognize their optimal application areas.
Practically apply interpolation, motion control, and path error correction.
Explain the principle of geometry processing and position control in NC controllers.
Classify numerical controls up to 5D path control and explain their application.
Understand and apply coordinate systems, reference points, path corrections, and zero point offsets.
Interpret and apply program keys according to DIN 66025.
Utilize subprogram technology, contour path programming, and cycle programming.
Explain the functions and differences of processor, post-processor, geometry processor, CLDATA processor, APT systems, and WOP programming systems.
Understand CAD-CAM couplings and utilize standardized interfaces (such as VDAFS, STEP, IGES).
Describe lathes, milling machines, and grinding machines in different designs, as well as electrical discharge cutting systems and their applications.
Classify main and auxiliary drives, recognize their dimensioning criteria, and apply them according to dynamic and process-technical requirements.
Analyze stiffness and compliance, design parameters, and cross-sectional shapes, and calculate and optimize frame components using the Finite Element Method (FEM).
Design, dimension, and calculate machine tool components.
Program machine tools using software and CAD-CAM modules like Fusion 360.
Understand and describe the basic principles and concepts of digital manufacturing and Industry 4.0.
Identify the essential technologies and methods of digital manufacturing and place them in the context of manufacturing systems.
Solve technical problems in the field of manufacturing systems analytically and creatively.
Apply theoretical knowledge in practice-oriented projects and implement it purposefully.
Prioritize the requirements of manufacturing processes and select suitable manufacturing systems.
Recognize technological innovations, acquire new knowledge independently, and continuously further their education.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of machine tools and their requirements and designs
Drive systems and guides of machine tools
Measurement systems and accuracy of machine tools
Dimensioning and calculation of drive systems
Static, dynamic, and thermal aspects of machine tool design
Application of the Finite Element Method (FEM) in machine tool design
Integrated CAD-CAM modules, Digital Manufacturing, and Industry 4.0
Numerical controls, NC programming, and NC programming practical course
Program keys and programming techniques according to DIN 66025
Understanding the interactions between manufacturing processes, manufacturing facilities, and other technical, economic, and environmental aspects
Development of skills for independent learning and acquisition of new knowledge, as well as adaptation to technological innovations and continuous further education
Evaluation of the economic and ecological effects of digital transformation in manufacturing
assessment_rules: The prerequisite for admission to the examination is successful participation in the practical course. Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written examination.
